beth (devex): Heads up from today's instructor-led onboarding: sampleapp started sending requests under a stale org key that lived in my macOS keychain. I had RW_PROJECT_KEY exported but the app picked the keychain entry first.

sam (sdk): that sounds like the auth resolver changed order when we upgraded the keyring lib. Do you have the exact repro?

beth (devex): yep: `export RW_PROJECT_KEY=proj_test_1; ./sampleapp demo` -> requests show workspace=org-staging in logs. Checked `security find-generic-password -a beth -s redwood` and saw the org token there.

ivan (platform): ugh. earlier contract was env -> config file (~/.redwood/creds) -> system keychain -> metadata. Looks like the library now returns system keychain before env if a config file exists.

sam (sdk): that's a regression. Intentional order is explicit env first. I'll roll a patch to enforce env precedence and add explicit checks in the resolver.

nora (security): also important: our rotate tool writes to the system keychain without namespacing. If multiple projects use the same OS account, they clobber each other. We need namespaced keys like `redwood:project:<proj_id>` and `redwood:org:<org_id>` and audit on write.

beth (devex): UX ask: can we surface a one-line startup diagnostic when conflicting sources exist? e.g., `Conflicting credentials found: RW_PROJECT_KEY (env) and redwood:org token (keychain). Using RW_PROJECT_KEY. See <link>`

sam (sdk): will do. Also adding a small `rw auth doctor` devtool that prints effective credential order, lists detected tokens (masking values), and suggests cleanup steps like `security delete-generic-password -s redwood -a <user>`.

ivan (platform): we should also update the sampleapp Dockerfile to explicitly unset system-level envs and ensure images don't accidentally pick up host keyrings in buildpacks. CI can run a quickcheck that fails if any `RW_*ORG*` env appears in Dockerfile or if credential files are copied into images.

nora (security): please add a migration note for power users who have existing keychain entries; include a helper script to rename legacy unscoped items to namespaced keys and preserve audit logs. Rotations that overwrite legacy keys should require `--force` and log the previous key fingerprint.

sam (sdk): PR opened: https://git.redwood/sdks/pull/998 - enforces env-first precedence, adds keychain namespacing API, and a small unit test matrix for macOS keychain / linux-secret-store / windows-cred-manager. Leaving TODO for `rw auth doctor`.

deploy-bot: canary-preview: PR 998 passed unit tests, queued for canary deploy. :rocket:

sam (sdk): follow-up: will add a warning metric `auth.conflict_detected` so we can see how often this trips onboarding. beth, can you add a short note in the quickstart that recommends running `rw auth doctor` when onboarding fails?

beth (devex): will do. Closing after PR merge + quickstart update + CI dockerfile lint. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
